L1-L2.title: Retain incomplete managed-shutdown evidence until reconciliation

L3.title: Fail closed when installer repair cannot read a candidate image path

L5.title: Include FP32 head-logit mode in the durable engine identity

L6.title: Preserve paused-owner power metadata during uninstall

L1.claim: Stop-ManagedProcess returns success when a stop-event launch's shutdown report is missing, unreadable or wrong-launch (`graceful_unreported`), and after forced termination (`graceful_wait_expired`, `graceful_nonzero_exit`, `terminated`, `signal_failed`); only an explicit incomplete report throws
L1.rationale: Fail-open on absent evidence is real. After C-ROLLBACK, C-TXSCOPE, C-RECOMPUTE and C-PROCESS, the only reachable loss is the checkpoints of a candidate whose install never completed, deleted by transaction rollback/repair after an unclean candidate stop. That loss is cache-only, and the incumbent cannot consume a candidate's checkpoints anyway. Fixing it changes package bytes and therefore N, forcing a rebuild, re-cut and re-qualification of all three lanes: disproportionate to a bounded cache loss. Next release: treat a missing or invalid report and forced termination of a stop-event launch as incomplete, keep runtime.json and the candidate cache, and require an explicit operator reconcile. Add a red→green Windows test.

L2.claim: A refused final save is not sticky across a later Start, so a later clean Stop can permit transaction rollback
L2.rationale: Same asset and consequence class as L1: candidate cache inside an unfinished install transaction, recomputable. The refused sessions were never saved, so a later rollback deletes nothing that the refusal was protecting beyond the candidate cache. Fix together with L1.

L3.claim: Repair's quiescence census drops processes whose ExecutablePath is unreadable when state no longer names the candidate
L3.rationale: Under C-LOCKS a surviving candidate makes cleanup and the incumbent restart fail visibly. The installer runs elevated, so a blank ExecutablePath for the lane's own task child needs a protected or foreign-session process. No real-Windows evidence shows one; mythos U2 records the same gap. Next release: fail closed on blank-path processes named like the server, matching Control-Release.ps1:562-579.

L4.claim: Export retirement is not exception-safe if allocating the retirement command throws
L4.rationale: The code is unchanged since F2. The P15 sequence reviewed it, so this is a gap in a file outside the delta. Triggering it needs `std::bad_alloc` for a small host allocation, i.e. process-wide memory exhaustion. The server is already failing then, and the controller's stop timeout ends in forced termination. Next release: reserve the retirement node before taking the lease, or retire inline on failure.

L5.claim: `engine_identity()` omits `fp32_head_logits`, so the checkpoint fingerprint disagrees when the opt-in is enabled
L5.rationale: FP32 head logits is default OFF in every shipped profile. The packaged config is hash-asserted at Start (Control-Release.ps1:1079, 1169), so product users cannot enable it. With the opt-in on, restores would be refused, which fails closed: recompute, no corruption. Next release: one-line fix plus a restore test with the opt-in.

L6.claim: Uninstall removes the inner GPU-owner lease record while the outer lease has prior_paused=true, losing the prior power limit
L6.rationale: Uninstall is a deliberate whole-state-root removal. The card stays at the qualified cap, which is a safe limit, and an operator can restore the limit with nvidia-smi. Record it in the next release's uninstall notes and fix it with L1.
